context:
Start with the w1 timing measurement before committing to a placement -
the two options (PR-blocking-but-path-filtered vs post-merge-non-blocking)
have different cost/latency tradeoffs and the runtime number should drive
the choice, not a preference. If path-filtered into pr.yml, reuse the
path-filter-group mechanism being added by
pr-gate-package-and-audit-promotion rather than building a second,
divergent filtering mechanism.
description:
`make parity-check` (Makefile:930-937) regenerates the CLI↔explorer
visualization JSON fixtures under `tests/parity/fixtures/` and diffs them
against the checked-in copies, catching drift between the Python
implementations and the fixtures the Vitest suite asserts against. The
`parity` job in `test.yml` runs this (and the Vitest suite) but is
explicitly excluded from develop PRs by its own `if:` condition
(test.yml:450: `github.base_ref != 'develop'`), and it is not part of
`develop-post-merge.yml`'s auto-revert safety net either
(`develop-post-merge.yml` only runs `ci-lint`, `ci-test`, and
`explorer-tokens`, :20-69). So a viz/explorer change that drifts the
fixtures can land on develop and stay unblocked until the next release PR
to `main`, where `parity` finally runs.

anti_patterns.dont: add parity-check to every develop PR unconditionally if it is expensive
anti_patterns.instead: path-filter it or move it to post-merge.
anti_patterns.why: most PRs never touch viz/explorer code

anti_patterns.instead: extend the same classifier config rather than writing a parallel one.

anti_patterns.dont: silently drop the Release v* PR skip when porting logic from test.yml:450
anti_patterns.instead: carry the same exemption into whichever new job you add.
anti_patterns.why: that condition exists so curation-only version-bump PRs aren't blocked on fixture regen

preserves.behavior: Release v* PRs keep skipping parity per the existing condition (test.yml:450) if that same skip logic is reused for the new job.
develop-post-merge.yml's existing lint and fast-test jobs (develop-post-merge.yml:20-56) are unaffected if w1 chooses post-merge placement - parity-check is an additional job, not a replacement.
test.yml's parity job continues to run on the release/main PR path unchanged - this item adds a develop-side ring, it does not replace the existing main-release check.

prior_art.concept: Makefile:930-937 parity-check target — reuse as-is, no new Make target needed
develop-post-merge.yml:20-56 lint/fast-test jobs — reuse as the post-merge placement pattern if w1 chooses that option
test.yml:445-450 parity job condition (Release v* exemption) — reuse the exemption logic for whichever new job is added

verifications.description: Baseline runtime measured before placement decision
verifications.expected: wall-clock time recorded and cited in the PR/commit that implements w1

verifications.command: On a scratch branch: touch a change to a viz-generating Python module without regenerating tests/parity/fixtures, open a PR against develop, check the new job/ring
verifications.description: A deliberately stale fixture is caught on develop (not just on release PRs)
verifications.expected: new job fails (PR-blocking) or triggers auto-revert (post-merge), depending on w1's placement choice
no new required job runs, or it runs and passes trivially fast

work_units.notes:
DECISION: PR-blocking, path-filtered lane in pr.yml.

Measured: `time make parity-check` — real 0m0.87s (3 runs: 0.885s,
0.871s, 0.843s), consistently under 1s. `make parity-check` itself is
pure Python (regenerate fixtures into a tmpdir, `diff -r` against
tests/parity/fixtures/) — it does NOT run npm/vitest (that's a
separate step only in nightly.yml's/test.yml's `parity` job, out of
this TODO's scope per do_not_modify: tests/parity/generate_visualization_fixtures.py
and the nightly/test.yml jobs). This is comparable to or cheaper than
explorer-tokens (stdlib-only) once dependencies are already synced, so
per the TODO's own heuristic ("if cheap ... prefer path-filtering into
pr.yml as a develop-PR-blocking job") it goes into pr.yml, not
develop-post-merge.yml, as w1's "cheap" branch directs.

Reused the packaging path-filter-group mechanism added by
pr-gate-package-and-audit-promotion.yaml (that TODO's
`extra_group_keys()` generalization in path_filter_decision.py) rather
than inventing a second classifier: added a `viz:` group to
.github/path-filters.yml covering `results-explorer/**`,
`tests/parity/**`, `_project/scripts/explorer_pipeline/**`. This
required doing pr-gate-package-and-audit-promotion.yaml's w1
classifier extension first, which the dependency graph doesn't
enforce (deps.needs: [] on both TODOs) but the approach note calls
for by name — done in this session in package/audit order first.

KNOWN ISSUE FOUND (not caused by this change, fixtures/generator are
do_not_modify): `make parity-check` FAILS in this sandbox today —
`tests/parity/fixtures/geomean_ms.json`'s checked-in geomean value
(237.9081547062432) differs from a freshly-regenerated value
(237.9081547062434) by 2e-13 (a last-bit float rounding difference),
reproduced identically across 3 runs (deterministic, not flaky here).
Root cause is most likely a libm/transcendental-function (math.exp/
math.log, used by the geometric mean) precision difference between
this sandbox's environment and whatever environment last regenerated
the committed fixture (possibly GitHub Actions' own ubuntu-latest, in
which case this fixture may ALREADY be silently failing test.yml's
`parity` job on release PRs and nightly.yml's `parity` job — or it may
be sandbox-specific and clean on GHA). I did NOT touch
tests/parity/fixtures/ or generate_visualization_fixtures.py (out of
scope_limit; also do_not_modify). CONSEQUENCE: the new pr.yml
`parity-check` job as wired will likely fail on ITS FIRST RUN on any
real develop PR that touches a viz path, exactly like
medium-tier-ci-home.yaml's one known pre-existing failure. Recommend:
before merging, a human runs `make parity-check` on an actual GitHub
Actions ubuntu-latest runner (not this sandbox) to determine whether
this is sandbox-only or a real, currently-undetected fixture drift on
develop; if real, regenerate fixtures via `make parity-fixtures`
first (out of scope for me to do unilaterally). Original notes:
Run `time make parity-check` to get a baseline. If it is cheap
(comparable to the existing `explorer-tokens` job, which is
stdlib-only and lint-fast), prefer path-filtering it into pr.yml as
a develop-PR-blocking job gated on results-explorer/viz path changes
(extend `scripts/path_filter_decision.py` /
`.github/path-filters.yml` the same way
pr-gate-package-and-audit-promotion does for packaging paths - reuse
that filter-group pattern rather than inventing a second one). If it
is expensive (needs a Python env sync plus Vitest/npm install), place
it in `develop-post-merge.yml` instead, mirroring the existing
`lint`/`fast-test` jobs (develop-post-merge.yml:20-56) - non-blocking
to the PR but caught immediately post-merge with the auto-revert
path.

work_units.notes:
Done, then REVISED after review (2026-07-04): the job initially
landed wired into ci-required-result (skipped-counts-as-pass, the
package-smoke pattern), but review correctly flagged that shipping a
blocking gate that is known-red locally (the unexplained 2e-13
geomean_ms.json drift, see w1) risks hard-blocking every viz-touching
develop PR on arrival — including the PR introducing it — if the
drift reproduces on GitHub runners. DEMOTED to non-blocking in the
same change: the `parity-check` job keeps its viz path filter but now
has `continue-on-error: true` and is deliberately NOT in
`ci-required-result.needs` (PARITY_CHECK_RESULT env + aggregator
check removed). A failure shows red in the PR checks list without
blocking merge — same visibility model as the postgres/datafusion/
clickhouse sample jobs.

PROMOTION CRITERION (also recorded in the job comment in pr.yml and
pinned by tests/unit/workflows/test_pr_workflow_path_classifier.py::
test_parity_check_is_demoted_to_non_blocking): promote to the
required lane only after BOTH (1) one green run of this job on a real
GitHub runner, AND (2) a decision on the geomean_ms.json float drift
(comparison tolerance vs fixture regen — out of this TODO's scope,
fixtures/generator are do_not_modify). Promotion is mechanical: drop
continue-on-error, add parity-check to ci-required-result.needs +
PARITY_CHECK_RESULT env + a success-or-skipped check (copy the
package-smoke pattern), and flip the pinned demotion test to
package-smoke-style assertions.

Test.yml's own `parity` job
(main-release path) is untouched, still runs its Release-v*-PR skip
condition unchanged — pr.yml never sees a "Release v*"-titled PR
anyway (pr.yml only triggers on `pull_request: branches: [develop]`;
release PRs target `main` via test.yml), so the must_preserve/
anti-pattern about carrying that exemption forward does not actually
apply to this placement — noted here rather than silently ignored.
